## About the Specific Method/Constructor

The search results don't contain documentation specifically detailing a four-argument `getCleanNodeName` constructor in ZAP's `SiteNode` class. However, I found substantial context around the related concept of **data driven nodes (DDN)** and **context scoping** in ZAP.

## Context on Data Driven Nodes and Scoping

Data driven nodes are part of ZAP's "Structural Modifiers" feature. Structural Modifiers are controls which change how ZAP represents the structure of the application. The Sites tab shows ZAP's representation of the application. If it is not a good representation of the structure then ZAP will not be able to attack the application effectively.

The core purpose relates to how ZAP handles URLs containing data rather than structure. Some applications include data in URL paths. These URLs represent the same page but with different data, but by default ZAP will represent them as separate nodes. In ZAP terms these are 'data driven content' - URL parameters that contain data instead of representing part of the application structure.

Regarding context configuration, you can define structural parameters by adding the application to a Context and then configuring them via the Context Structure page.

## Related Scoping/Context Behavior

On the context scoping side, the ZAP `Context` class includes methods for scope determination. It gets the nodes from the site tree which are "In Scope," searching recursively starting from the root node. This should be used with care, as it is time-consuming, querying the database for every node in the Site Tree.

There have also been known issues around DDN context scoping, such as nested data-driven nodes. Errors appear in the form of warnings like "Unable to find path segment while inferring rule" from the ContextAccessRulesManager, appended with a «DDN» identifier.

## Recommendation

For the precise signature and behavior of the four-argument `SiteNode` constructor or the `getCleanNodeName` method (which handles cleaning node names in the context of data-driven scoping), I'd recommend consulting the **ZAP source code directly on GitHub** (`zaproxy/zaproxy` repository, in `org.zaproxy.zap.model.SiteNode` / `Context` / `StructuralNodeModifier` classes) or the official Javadoc, as these implementation-level details weren't captured in the search results.
